title: a16z Opens First Japan Office to Accelerate AI Economy
summary:
The former head of Microsoft Japan and Hewlett-Packard Japan will steer a new regional hub for one of Silicon Valley's most prominent venture capital firms. Andreessen Horowitz, also known as a16z, officially opened its first office in the country with Governor Koike in attendance to integrate its portfolio companies into the local industrial and innovation ecosystem.

The firm targets the growth of an AI-native economy by leveraging national capabilities in robotics, AI, cybersecurity, and defense. Hitoshi Yoshida's appointment as Head of Japan brings established relationships across government and business to facilitate closer ties between US and Japanese technology sectors.

selectedTweets.text:
a16z is officially in Japan, led by Hitoshi Yoshida as Head of Japan, with the opening of our Japan office.

It was an honor welcoming Governor Koike at the opening earlier today. Japan combines world-class industrial capabilities with growing innovation in AI, cybersecurity, robotics, and defense. By bringing our portfolio companies and the Japanese ecosystem together, we aim to accelerate Japan’s AI-native economy and strengthen the ties between Silicon Valley and Japan.

As the former President of Microsoft Japan and Hewlett-Packard Japan, Hitoshi brings decades of technology leadership and deep relationships across business, industry, and government. We’re thrilled to have him lead our efforts in Japan and look forward to doing great work in partnership with the Japanese technology community.

日本代表として吉田仁志を迎え、日本オフィスを開設できたことを大変心強く光栄に思います。日本は、世界有数の産業基盤と、AI・サイバーセキュリティ・ロボティクス・防衛などの分野における目覚ましいイノベーションを兼ね備えています。
我々はこれまでになかった機会を、日本の若い世代に提供していくことを目指します。日本のテクノロジーコミュニティの皆様と共に、日本の市場やエコシステムの発展に貢献していけることを楽しみにしています。
